South: front view with the face toward the camera, beak open, two teal eyes, both wings spread upward and four clawed legs splayed toward the viewer. East: a side profile facing right with a long thin tail trailing left, four slim clawed legs, one wing raised, a grey-blue neck and a hooked beak. North: rear view with the back of a pale crested skull, a scaled back, the tail running straight down toward the viewer and both wings spread up. The facings are on a checkerboard and nothing is baked in.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution: a pale grey-bone head with a small pale crest, two teal eyes and a long hooked beak open to show a pink tongue. observed.east.png: A true right-facing side profile. The head is pale with a crest and one teal eye, and the open beak is long and hooked. The neck is long and blue-grey. observed.north.png: Rear view: the back of the crested skull with no eyes visible, a scaled neck and spine, both wings spread up, four legs seen from behind and the tail running toward the camera. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the east view spans about two cells long. The body is roughly human height, with the wing tip above the human. At 32 px per cell the creature reads as a small dark winged silhouette with pink wings next to the human and the rat.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the crested skull, the spine, the wing backs and the tail toward the viewer. No eyes and no face.

ALIEN.seen: The six-limb plan (four walking legs plus separate wings) and the scaled beaked head rule out a pterosaur. It reads as an invented wyvern-like reptavian.

concerns.evidence: The candidate and adults share pebbled charcoal bodies, teal eyes beneath pale brow plates, hooked beaks, separate walking legs and the same ribbed wing construction. The visible palette difference does not make it read as a different species or artist.

In south.png the broad forehead and large teal eyes dominate the face, with much less cranial spiking than the adult south view. In east.png the head is conspicuously large relative to the compact torso, the legs are short and the tail is slender and extended. These are visible juvenile proportions; the south forelegs project toward the camera.

The measured height difference is visible, but the silhouettes explain it: south and north have upright necks and wing tips reaching high above the shoulders, while east has a forward-reaching neck and swept-back wings. The side view's head and torso retain comparable anatomical scale. The adult reference shows the same tall frontal/rear silhouettes and low side silhouette.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a winged creature seen from the front. It has two large leathery wings raised in a V, dark brown bony struts and reddish-purple membranes with darker mottling. The body is a round, pot-bellied red-brown mass heavily speckled with dark brown leopard-like spots. The head is a wrinkled dome with an open toothed mouth. The spotted tail curls up to the left, and two thin blue-violet legs hang down, ending in large dark hooked talons. East: a side profile facing right. The head is a domed, ridged, wrinkled skull with a toothed jaw and no eye visible. The body is pale tan and pot-bellied, with a purple wash over the back. A long plain pink-tan tail sweeps up and back. Two thin violet legs trail with hooked talons. The wings are lavender with maroon blotches. North: the rear. The back of the domed head shows as a ridged bulb, with no face or eyes. The body is tan and wrinkled, the plain tan tail curls around the left side, and the legs and talons hang down. The wing membranes are grey-violet with dark smoky mottling. Body colour and spotting differ clearly between south (dark-spotted red-brown) and east/north (plain tan).
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution. A V of spread bat wings, with red-purple membranes mottled darker and dark struts. The body and tail are densely spotted dark brown on a reddish ground. The head is a wrinkled dome with a grinning toothed mouth, and I see no distinct eyes. Violet legs end in big dark hooked talons. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: Right-facing profile. An eyeless, ridged, domed head with a toothed open jaw. The belly is pale tan and bulbous, with a purple-mauve dorsal wash. The tail is long, thin and unspotted. The near wing is large and lavender with maroon blotches, and the far wing is raised behind. Thin violet legs end in hooked talons. Clean alpha, painterly shading.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The back of the domed head is a ridged bulb, with a dark spine line running down between the wings. The body is tan and wrinkled, and the plain tan tail loops around the left side of the body. The wings are grey-violet with smoky dark mottling. Two legs with talons hang below. No face. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature spans about two cells wide and two cells tall next to the vanilla human, much larger than the human's body. At 32 px/cell it reads as a purple winged shape, larger than the rat and the human, and distinct from the brown ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult shyrack. The same pose and silhouette on all three facings, with pink-magenta wing membranes, a peach-flesh unspotted body, violet legs and a peach tail. The adult's palette is consistent across all three facings.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are angled views at the game camera. None is a rotated top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Wingspan and body size match across the facings. The code-measured spread is 11%, within 15%.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Anatomy and structures match and turn with the body, but the palette disagrees. South has a red-brown body and tail densely spotted dark brown, while east and north have a plain tan unspotted body and tail. The wing membrane hue shifts from red-purple on south to lavender with maroon blotches on east to grey-violet smoky on north.

SIGNATURE.seen: Large leathery bat wings and a toothed mouth are clear on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: The def names a bat-like body, and the eyeless wrinkled domed head, pot belly, long thin tail and taloned stilt legs read as a cave creature, not an ordinary bat.

CANON.seen: All canon lines are present. Body plan: hunched pot-belly, bat wings, no separate forelegs, thin hind legs, sinuous tail. Leathery purple-toned membranes with dark struts and no feathers. STYLE.seen: Painterly shading, wrinkled skin, veined membranes, no keyline, not cute.

OURS.seen: Own commissioned art that matches the owner-kept sibling's anatomy. Not vanilla or donor.

edits.change: One fixed coat for every facing: red-brown body, belly and tail ground colour (warm russet, mid value), covered in dense dark-brown leopard-like rosette spots on body, haunches, neck and tail. The south, east and north views all carry this same ground colour and the same spot pattern, so the animal keeps one coat as it turns.

One fixed wing-membrane scheme for every facing: wine-red membrane with purple mottling and darker plum blotches between the wing fingers. The same wine-purple hue and the same mottling appear on south, east and north. Wing bones and finger struts are a darker red-brown.

Lighting is one soft top-left light on all three views. It changes only the shading of form (lighter top planes, darker undersides); the hue, saturation and spot density of the coat stay the same on every view. The east and north views are as red-brown and as spotted as the south view.

The three views show one individual, drawn together as a facing sheet: south is the front view with eyes toward the viewer, east is the side view in profile, north is the rear view seen from behind, showing the back, folded wing roots, haunches and the spotted tail, with the eyes hidden. Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette.

invariants: Body plan: large bat-like cave creature, leathery wings folded at the sides when walking, sturdy limbs, long spotted tail, sharp teeth visible in the front view

Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges, value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette, transparent background. Top-down three-quarter game view, one soft light from the top left on all three views. Body: heavy, hunched, walking on sturdy hind legs and the knuckles of its wing arms, a broad chest, a short thick neck, a large head with big ears, a wide mouth showing sharp teeth, and a long tail. Leathery wings are folded against the flanks. Coat, identical on every facing: the body, belly, haunches, neck, head and tail are warm red-brown, mid value, covered in dense dark-brown leopard-like rosette spots, the same spot pattern and the same density on the body and the tail in all three views. Wing membranes, identical on every facing: wine-red with purple mottling and darker plum blotches between the wing fingers, with the wing bones and finger struts in a darker red-brown. The south view is the front view, eyes toward the viewer, face and chest visible. The east view is the side view in profile, head to the right, with the spotted flank, folded wing and tail visible. The north view is the rear view, seen from behind: back, folded wing roots, haunches and spotted tail, with the eyes hidden. Lighting changes only the shading of form on each view; the hue, saturation, spot pattern and membrane colour stay constant, so all three views read as one animal with one coat. Same body size and proportions on all three views.
